chain.label: FAA duty-time rules permitted long duty day; no special check-airman duty limits
chain.trigger: existing FAA pilot flight and duty time regulations permitted the long and demanding day experienced by the accident pilots

chain.label: Pilots fatigued after 14+ hr duty day, 5th leg, captain also performing check-airman OE duties
chain.trigger: the pilots had flown 8.35 hours, made five landings, been on duty more than 14 hours, and been awake more than 16 hours

caused_by.evidence: existing FAA pilot flight and duty time regulations permitted the long and demanding day...which resulted in their fatigued condition and degraded pilot decision-making

chain.label: Runway 28 rapidly recontaminated with wet snow/ice after plowing, braking action reported probably nil
chain.trigger: moderate-to-heavy snow fell after the snow removal operations were completed, and the runway conditions deteriorated

chain.label: TVC operations supervisor gave ambiguous, imprecise braking-action phraseology and did not confirm nil report when queried

caused_by.evidence: he did not have time to do a full field condition measurement and report before the accident airplane arrived

chain.label: Pilots decided to continue and land at TVC without performing the required landing distance assessment

caused_by.evidence: the poor decision-making shown by the accident pilots...likely reflected the effects of fatigue
continuing reports of deteriorating weather and runway conditions during the approach
the TVC operations supervisor's use of ambiguous and unspecific radio phraseology...likely affected the captain's decision to continue the approach
